```{r, define spell_nr}

spell_nr <- function(x){
  if (x <= 9){
    as.character(english::english(x))
  } else{
    x
  } 
}
```

```{r, Read data}
# Excel sheet of the spots with details
spots <- read_excel(here("data", "datasheet_landsurvey.xlsx"),sheet ="spots")


# Clean the sighting data and import

full <- readRDS("./temp/full.rds")

obis_comp <- readRDS("./temp/obis.rds")





# Set active spots as variable
active_spots <- spots %>%  
  filter(spot_name != "MedSteps" & spot_name != "WestSide") %>% 
  select(spot_name)



odontoceti <- c("common_dolphin", "striped_dolphin", "bottlenose_dolphin", "delphinidae")
mysteciti <- c("fin_whale")

active <- data %>% filter(spot_name %in% active_spots$spot_name)

clean <- active %>% select(spot_name, spot_clean) %>%  distinct(spot_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

active_spots <- active_spots %>% left_join(clean, by = "spot_name")
```

```{r, Effort analysis}
#|include: false

effort <- effort_log %>% 
  mutate(date = dmy(date)) %>% 
  filter(date > "2026-05-28") %>% 
  mutate(across(c(observation_start, observation_end),
                ~ hms::as_hms(.))) %>% 
  filter(!grepl("off_effort", survey_id)) %>% 
  mutate(effort_time = as.duration(observation_end - observation_start))

er <- data %>%  
  filter(spot_name %in% active_spots$spot_name) %>% 
  summarise(min_group = min(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_group = max(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_group = mean(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_group = median(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_group = sd(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_dis = min(distance, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_dis = max(distance, na.rm = TRUE),
            sightings = n(),
            .by = "spot_name") %>%
  left_join(effort %>%
              group_by(spot_name) %>% 
  summarise(hours = sum(effort_time)/60^2), by = "spot_name") %>% 
  mutate(per_hour = round(sightings/hours, 2)) %>% 
  mutate(group_range = paste(min_group, "-", max_group)) %>% 
  select(spot_name, sightings, hours, per_hour, min_dis, max_dis, group_range, mean_group, median_group, sd_group) %>% 
  arrange(desc(per_hour))


total_land <- effort %>% 
  summarise(
    surveys = n()
  )

species <- data %>%  
  filter(spot_name %in% active_spots$spot_name) %>% 
  summarise(max_group = max(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_group = min(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_dis = max(distance, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_dis = min(distance, na.rm = TRUE),
            sightings = n(),
            .by = "species")  %>% 
  arrange(desc(sightings))
```

```{r, Overview Table by Spot}
library(dplyr)
library(tinytable)

## --- helpers -----------------------------------------------------------------
## NA (not Inf) for all-missing subsets; en-dash range, em-dash for empty.
smin <- function(x) { x <- x[!is.na(x)]; if (length(x)) min(x) else NA_real_ }
smax <- function(x) { x <- x[!is.na(x)]; if (length(x)) max(x) else NA_real_ }
rng  <- function(a, b) {
  ifelse(is.na(a) | is.na(b), "—",
         ifelse(a == b, as.character(a),
                paste0(a, " – ", b)))
}
## NA/NaN-safe numeric formatting (single-sighting species -> SD is NA)
fmt  <- function(x, d) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), x))

pretty_species <- function(x) {
  map <- c(common_dolphin = "Common Dolphin",
           delphinidae     = "Delphinidae",
           fin_whale       = "Fin Whale",
           unidentified    = "Unidentified")
  out  <- unname(map[x])
  miss <- is.na(out)
  out[miss] <- tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", x[miss]))
  out
}

active <- data %>% filter(spot_name %in% active_spots$spot_name)

clean <- active %>% select(spot_name, spot_clean) %>%  distinct(spot_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

## --- 1. spot-level summary (== your `er` table) ------------------------------
spot_sum <- active %>%
  summarise(
    sightings    = n(),
    d_min        = round(smin(distance)),
    d_max        = round(smax(distance)),
    g_min        = smin(group_size),
    g_max        = smax(group_size),
    g_mean       = mean(group_size,   na.rm = TRUE),
    g_median     = median(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    g_sd         = sd(group_size,     na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = spot_name
  ) %>% 
  left_join(
    effort %>% group_by(spot_name) %>%
      summarise(hours = sum(effort_time) / 60^2, .groups = "drop"),
    by = "spot_name"
  ) %>%
  mutate(per_hour = round(sightings / hours, 2),
         hours    = round(hours, 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(per_hour))            # spot ordering = descending encounter rate

spot_sum <- spot_sum %>%  left_join(clean, by = "spot_name")

## --- 2. species-level split within each spot ---------------------------------
sp_sum <- active %>%
  summarise(
    sightings = n(),
    d_min     = round(smin(distance)),
    d_max     = round(smax(distance)),
    g_min     = smin(group_size),
    g_max     = smax(group_size),
    g_mean    = mean(group_size,   na.rm = TRUE),
    g_median  = median(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    g_sd      = sd(group_size,     na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(spot_clean, species)
  ) %>%
  arrange(match(spot_clean, spot_sum$spot_clean), desc(sightings))

## --- 3. build interleaved display rows ---------------------------------------
spot_order <- tibble(spot_clean = spot_sum$spot_clean,
                     .ord = seq_along(spot_sum$spot_clean))

spot_rows <- spot_sum %>%
  transmute(
    spot_clean,
    label                = spot_clean,
    Sightings            = as.character(sightings),
    `Distance range (m)` = rng(d_min, d_max),
    `Group range`        = rng(g_min, g_max),
    Hours                = sprintf("%.1f", hours),
    `Sightings·h⁻¹`      = sprintf("%.2f", per_hour),
    `Mean group`         = fmt(g_mean, 2),
    `Median group`       = fmt(g_median, 1),
    `SD group`           = fmt(g_sd, 2),
    .is_spot = TRUE, .sub = 0
  )

sp_rows <- sp_sum %>%
  transmute(
    spot_clean,
    label                = paste0("\u2003", pretty_species(species)),   # indent species
    Sightings            = as.character(sightings),
    `Distance range (m)` = rng(d_min, d_max),
    `Group range`        = rng(g_min, g_max),
    Hours = "", `Sightings·h⁻¹` = "",
    `Mean group`         = fmt(g_mean, 2),
    `Median group`       = fmt(g_median, 1),
    `SD group`           = fmt(g_sd, 2),
    .is_spot = FALSE
  ) %>%
  group_by(spot_clean) %>% mutate(.sub = row_number()) %>% ungroup()

combined <- bind_rows(spot_rows, sp_rows) %>%
  left_join(spot_order, by = "spot_clean") %>%
  arrange(.ord, .sub)

spot_pos <- which(combined$.is_spot)          # row indices to emphasise

disp <- combined %>%
  select("Location / Taxon" = label, Sightings,
         "On-effort hours" = Hours,
         "Sightings per hour" = `Sightings·h⁻¹`,
         "Distance from observer" = `Distance range (m)`,
         "Range"  = `Group range`,
         "Mean"   = `Mean group`,
         "Median" = `Median group`,
         "SD"     = `SD group`)

## --- 4. render ---------------------------------------------------------------
## columns: 1 label | 2 Sightings | 3 Hours | 4 rate | 5 Distance | 6-9 Group block
overview_tbl <- tt(
  disp, width = c(4.7, 2, 2.3, 3, 4, 2.5, 2, 2, 2)
) %>%
  group_tt(j = list("Group Size" = 6:9)) %>%      # spanner over Range/Mean/Median/SD
  style_tt(j = 2:9, align = "c") %>%
  style_tt(i = spot_pos, bold = TRUE, background = "#212842", color = "white") %>%
  style_tt(i = -1:0, bold = TRUE)                 # bold spanner + header rows
#overview_tbl


```


```{r}
#| include: false
#| output: false

effort <- effort_log %>%
  filter(!str_detect(survey_id, "off_effort")) %>%
  mutate(date = dmy(date)) %>% 
  filter(date > "2026-05-28") %>% 
  mutate(
    duration_min = as.numeric(difftime(observation_end, observation_start,
                                        units = "mins"))
  )

clean <- data %>% select(spot_name, spot_clean) %>%  distinct(spot_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

effort <- effort %>% left_join(clean, by = "spot_name")
 
# ---- 3. Detections: keep on-effort sightings -------------------------------
sightings <- detection %>%
  filter(on_effort == 1)

 
# ---- 4. Sightings & individuals per scan -----------------------------------
per_scan <- sightings %>%
  group_by(survey_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sightings   = n(),
    n_individuals = sum(group_size, na.rm = TRUE),  # one NA group size -> 0
    .groups = "drop"
  )
 
# Join back onto the full effort table; scans with no sighting become 0 (NOT NA)
effort <- effort %>%
  left_join(per_scan, by = "survey_id") %>%
  mutate(
    n_sightings   = replace_na(n_sightings, 0),
    n_individuals = replace_na(n_individuals, 0)
  )
 
# ---- 5. SPUE by spot -------------------------------------------------------
spue_by_spot <- effort %>%
  group_by(spot_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    scans        = n(),
    effort_hours = sum(duration_min, na.rm = TRUE) / 60,
    sightings    = sum(n_sightings),
    individuals  = sum(n_individuals),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    spue_per_scan   = sightings / scans,        # headline SPUE
    sightings_per_h = sightings / effort_hours, # encounter rate
    indiv_per_h     = individuals / effort_hours
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(scans))
 
# ---- 6. SPUE overall -------------------------------------------------------
spue_overall <- effort %>%
  summarise(
    spot_clean    = "TOTAL",
    scans        = n(),
    effort_hours = sum(duration_min, na.rm = TRUE) / 60,
    sightings    = sum(n_sightings),
    individuals  = sum(n_individuals)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    spue_per_scan   = sightings / scans,
    sightings_per_h = sightings / effort_hours,
    indiv_per_h     = individuals / effort_hours
  )
 
spue_summary <- bind_rows(spue_by_spot, spue_overall)
 
# ---- 7. Report & export ----------------------------------------------------
spue_report <- spue_summary %>%
  mutate(across(c(effort_hours, spue_per_scan, sightings_per_h, indiv_per_h),
                ~ round(.x, 3)))
 
#print(spue_report, n = Inf)
```

```{r, Distance function and test}
 #|include: false
 #|echo: false
 #|output: false
 #|fig-show: hide

library(Distance)

pool_dis <- readRDS(here("temp", "pool_dis.rds"))
trunc <- 8000
conversion.factor <- convert_units("Metre", NULL, "square metre")

# Overall detection function (pooled)
d.hn <- ds(data=pool_dis %>% filter(!is.na(pool_dis$size)), key="hn", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=trunc)
d.hr <- ds(data=pool_dis %>% filter(!is.na(pool_dis$size)), key="hr", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=trunc)


# Significant is good so it does not fit the data
gof_hn <- gof_ds(d.hn, plot = FALSE)

# P value is not significant, good
gof_hr <- gof_ds(d.hr, plot = FALSE)

# height as a covariate
d.ht <- ds(data=pool_dis %>% filter(!is.na(pool_dis$size)), key="hr", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=trunc, formula = ~height)
# Region as covariate
d.ss <- ds(data=pool_dis %>% filter(!is.na(pool_dis$size)), key="hr", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=trunc, formula = ~sea_state)
#Region and height
d.wh <- ds(data=pool_dis %>% filter(!is.na(pool_dis$size)), key="hr", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=trunc, formula =~wave_height)
d.ws <- ds(data=pool_dis %>% filter(!is.na(pool_dis$size)), key="hr", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=trunc, formula = ~wind_speed)
d.gl <- ds(data=pool_dis %>% filter(!is.na(pool_dis$size)), key="hr", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=trunc, formula = ~glare)


# Write summary table
model_tab <- summarize_ds_models(d.hn, d.hr, d.ht, d.ss, d.wh, d.ws, d.gl, output = "plain")

# Summary of the best model and abundance and density estimates
sum_ht <- summary(d.ht)


```

```{r, Distance per spot}
dis <- readRDS(here("temp", "dis.rds"))


# Europa Point ------

              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=4500)

eu.AIC <- AIC(eu.hn, eu.hr)

# Significant is good so it does not fit the data

# P value is not significant, good
gof_hr_eu <- gof_ds(eu.hr, plot = FALSE)

# covariates
eu.gl <- ds(data=europa %>% filter(!is.na(size)), key="hr", adjustment= NULL,
              transect="point", convert_units=conversion.factor, truncation=4500, formula = ~glare)

model_europa <- summarize_ds_models(eu.hn, eu.hr, eu.gl, eu.ss, eu.wh, eu.ws, output = "plain")
```

```{r, Clean ds data}
 #|include: false


# # Pooled data

pool_group_dens <- sum_ht$dht$clusters$D %>%
  transmute(Label,
            "Density (km⁻²)"   = Estimate * 1e6,
            "SE (km⁻²)" = se * 1e6,
            "LCL (km⁻²)" = lcl * 1e6,
            "UCL (km⁻²)" = ucl * 1e6,
            CV = cv)

pool_indiv_dens <- d.ht$dht$individuals$D %>%
  transmute(Label,
            "Density (km⁻²)"   = Estimate * 1e6,
            "SE (km⁻²)" = se * 1e6,
            "LCL (km⁻²)" = lcl * 1e6,
            "UCL (km⁻²)" = ucl * 1e6,
            CV = cv)
# 
# # Abundance

pool <- sum_ht          # <- single pooled fit; change if d.ht is the intended one

# n of groups per stratum (+ Total) from the clusters summary
n_tbl <- pool$dht$clusters$summary %>% transmute(Label = Region, n_groups = n)

# helper: pull a D or N block, tag columns, keep Label as the key
pull_block <- function(df, scale = 1) {
  df %>% transmute(Label,
                   Estimate = Estimate * scale,
                   SE = se * scale,
                   LCL = lcl * scale,
                   UCL = ucl * scale,
                   CV  = cv)
}

grp_dens <- pull_block(pool$dht$clusters$D,    1e6)   # km^-2
ind_dens <- pull_block(pool$dht$individuals$D, 1e6)   # km^-2
grp_abun <- pull_block(pool$dht$clusters$N,    1)     # counts
ind_abun <- pull_block(pool$dht$individuals$N, 1)     # counts

pool_overview_tbl <- n_tbl %>%
  left_join(grp_dens, by = "Label") %>%
  left_join(ind_dens, by = "Label", suffix = c(".gd", ".id")) %>%
  left_join(grp_abun, by = "Label") %>%
  left_join(ind_abun, by = "Label", suffix = c(".ga", ".ia")) %>%
  rename(Station = Label)

# rename to the exact column set your per-spot table used
names(pool_overview_tbl) <- c(
  "Station", "n of Groups",
  "Group Dens. Estimate","Group Dens. SE","Group Dens. LCL","Group Dens. UCL","Group Dens. CV",
  "Indiv. Dens. Estimate","Indiv. Dens. SE","Indiv. Dens. LCL","Indiv. Dens. UCL","Indiv. Dens. CV",
  "Group Abun. Estimate","Group Abun. SE","Group Abun. LCL","Group Abun. UCL","Group Abun. CV",
  "Indiv. Abun. Estimate","Indiv. Abun. SE","Indiv. Abun. LCL","Indiv. Abun. UCL","Indiv. Abun. CV"
)

pooled_tbl <- as.data.frame(pool_overview_tbl, check.names = FALSE)
colnames(pooled_tbl) <- c("Station","n of Groups", rep(c("Estimate","SE","LCL","UCL","CV"), 4))

pool_dens_tbl <- pooled_tbl[, c(1, 2, 3:12)]
names(pool_dens_tbl) <- c("Station", "n of Groups",
                          rep(c("Estimate","SE","LCL","UCL","CV"), 2))

pool_abun_tbl <- pooled_tbl[, c(1, 2, 13:22)]
names(pool_abun_tbl) <- c("Station", "n of Groups",
                          rep(c("Estimate","SE","LCL","UCL","CV"), 2))
```

```{r, Spot overview table}
 #|include: false

d.models <- list(
  "Prince George" = bf.prince,
  "Europa Point"       = bf.europa,
  "Sandy Bay"     = bf.sandy
)

extract_model <- function(model, station){
  cl <- model$dht$clusters
  ind <- model$dht$individuals
  tibble(
    Station        = station,
    n_groups       = cl$summary$n,
    # --- group (cluster) density ---
    group_dens_es  = cl$D$Estimate,
    group_dens_se  = cl$D$se,
    group_dens_lcl = cl$D$lcl,
    group_dens_ucl = cl$D$ucl,
    group_dens_cv  = cl$D$cv,
    # --- individual density ---
    indiv_dens_es  = ind$D$Estimate,
    indiv_dens_se  = ind$D$se,
    indiv_dens_lcl = ind$D$lcl,
    indiv_dens_ucl = ind$D$ucl,
    indiv_dens_cv  = ind$D$cv,
    # --- group (cluster) abundance ---
    group_abun_es  = cl$N$Estimate,
    group_abun_se  = cl$N$se,
    group_abun_lcl = cl$N$lcl,
    group_abun_ucl = cl$N$ucl,
    group_abun_cv  = cl$N$cv,
    # --- individual abundance ---
    indiv_abun_es  = ind$N$Estimate,
    indiv_abun_se  = ind$N$se,
    indiv_abun_lcl = ind$N$lcl,
    indiv_abun_ucl = ind$N$ucl,
    indiv_abun_cv  = ind$N$cv
  )
}

model_overview_tbl <- imap_dfr(d.models, extract_model)

clean_overview_tbl <- model_overview_tbl %>% 
  transmute(
  Station = Station,
  "n of Groups" = n_groups,

  # --- Group density (km^-2) ---
  "Group Dens. Estimate" = group_dens_es  * 1e6,
  "Group Dens. SE"       = group_dens_se  * 1e6,
  "Group Dens. LCL"      = group_dens_lcl * 1e6,
  "Group Dens. UCL"      = group_dens_ucl * 1e6,
  "Group Dens. CV"       = group_dens_cv,          

  # --- Individual density (km^-2) ---
  "Indiv. Dens. Estimate" = indiv_dens_es  * 1e6,
  "Indiv. Dens. SE"       = indiv_dens_se  * 1e6,
  "Indiv. Dens. LCL"      = indiv_dens_lcl * 1e6,
  "Indiv. Dens. UCL"      = indiv_dens_ucl * 1e6,
  "Indiv. Dens. CV"       = indiv_dens_cv,          

  # --- Group abundance (counts: no unit conversion) ---
  "Group Abun. Estimate" = group_abun_es,
  "Group Abun. SE"       = group_abun_se,
  "Group Abun. LCL"      = group_abun_lcl,
  "Group Abun. UCL"      = group_abun_ucl,
  "Group Abun. CV"       = group_abun_cv,

  # --- Individual abundance (counts: no unit conversion) ---
  "Indiv. Abun. Estimate" = indiv_abun_es,
  "Indiv. Abun. SE"       = indiv_abun_se,
  "Indiv. Abun. LCL"      = indiv_abun_lcl,
  "Indiv. Abun. UCL"      = indiv_abun_ucl,
  "Indiv. Abun. CV"       = indiv_abun_cv
)

dens_tbl <- clean_overview_tbl[, c(1, 2, 3:12)]
names(dens_tbl) <- c("Station", "n of Groups",
                          rep(c("Estimate","SE","LCL","UCL","CV"), 2))


abun_tbl <- clean_overview_tbl[, c(1, 2, 13:22)]
names(abun_tbl) <- c("Station", "n of Groups",
                          rep(c("Estimate","SE","LCL","UCL","CV"), 2))
```

This study applied point-transect distance sampling to assess the distribution and density of small cetaceans within the BGTW. A modified point-transect protocol, adapted from approaches primarily used for birds and larger cetaceans [@bucklandIntroductionDistanceSampling2001], was implemented for land-based surveys. The following results describe the observed cetacean occurrence, spatial distribution, and density estimates across the study area.

## Survey Results
In total `r total_land$surveys` land-based surveys were conducted, resulting in `r round(sum(er$hours), 2)` total on-effort hours and 58 off-effort hours over `r length(unique(effort$date))` survey days. `r length(data$survey_id)` cetacean sightings were recorded in this sampling period, of which `r sum(data$on_effort)` were on-effort and `r spell_nr(sum(!data$on_effort))` off-effort. Of these, `r by_familiy$odontoceti` sightings were Odontoceti, including `r by_species$common_dolphin` sightings of common dolphins, `r by_species$delphinidae` sightings of unidentified dolphins where the species could not certainly be defined and `r spell_nr(by_familiy$mysteciti)` Mysticeti sightings of  Fin whales (*Balaenoptera physalus*). For `r spell_nr(by_species$unidentified)` sightings the species could not be reliably determined and were recorded as unidentified (@fig-sight_map, Figure S15). The group size for land-based sightings ranged from `r min(data$group_size, na.rm = TRUE)` to `r max(data$group_size, na.rm = TRUE)` (mean = `r round(mean(data$group_size, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`, median = `r round(median(data$group_size, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`, SD = ±`r round(sd(data$group_size, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`). 

![All sightings collected from land-based surveys between `r format(min(full$date.x), "%d %b %Y")` and `r format(max(full$date.x), "%d %b %Y")`. The sightings were recorded from three different locations, Europa Point, Sandy Bay and Prince George's Battery (indicated as triangles).](figures/sightings_legend.png){#fig-sight_map}


The overview of sightings (@tbl-overview) revealed variation in minimum and maximum sighting distances and group sizes among sampling locations. The farthest sighting occurred at a distance of `r round(max(er$max_dis)/1000, 2)` km from the observation platform. Despite equal on-effort observation time across all sampling locations, the number of sightings differed strongly among locations. The most frequently recorded species was the common dolphin (n = `r species$sightings[1]`), followed by unidentified dolphins (n = `r species$sightings[2]`). Unidentified dolphins accounted for the most distant sightings, recorded at approximately `r round(max(species$max_dis/1000), 2)` km (@tbl-overview).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-overview
#| tbl-cap: "Statistics per observation platforms over the sampling period. Pilot studies were excluded in this table. Distance is calculated from the respective observation platform."

overview_tbl
```

Most of the sightings were recorded at Europa Point, covering mainly the southern side (n = `r max(per_spot$sightings)`). Sighting frequency varied over the course of the day, showing a bimodal distribution with peaks in the morning and afternoon and a reduction around midday (Figure S16 C).


## Spatial Distribution
SPUE differed significantly among the three stations (Kruskal–Wallis χ² = `r round(as.numeric(SPUE_kru$statistic),2)`, df = `r as.numeric(SPUE_kru$parameter)`, p = `r round(SPUE_kru$p.value,3)`) and was highest at Europa Point (@tbl-spue_report, @fig-SPUE). Pairwise comparisons (Dunn's test, Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted) confirmed that Europa Point differed from both Prince George (p = `r round(SPUE_dunn$res[1,4],3)`) and Sandy Bay (p = `r round(SPUE_dunn$res[2,4],3)`), while Prince George and Sandy Bay did not differ.

![Sightings per Unit Effort (SPUE) showed a significant difference between Europa Point and Prince George and Europa Point and Sandy Bay, using Kruksal-Wallis and Dunn's test.](figures/SPUE.png){#fig-SPUE}

The kernel density surface, weighted by group size and derived from identified common dolphin and unidentified delphinid sightings (fin whales excluded), identified a single concentration of occurrence at the southern tip of the peninsula (approximately 36.09–36.11 °N, 5.34–5.37 °W; @fig-kde_map). The 50% isopleth enclosed most of the southern sector, while the 95% isopleth extended around the peninsula across all three sectors.

![The Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) of the sightings collected from land-based surveys between `r format(min(full$date.x), "%d %b %Y")` and `r format(max(full$date.x), "%d %b %Y")`. The KDE was calculated using group size as a weight variable. The highest density was found around the south western tip of the peninsula (approximately 36.09–36.11 °N, 5.34–5.37 °W; ~5 km²). Color of grid represents the density Utilisazion distribution.](figures/density_map.png){#fig-kde_map}

### Systematic vs. opportunistic sampling
Comparison with opportunistic records revealed a pronounced spatial mismatch between the two data sources (@fig-obis, @tbl-obis_comp). Of 200 *Delphinus delphis* records retrieved from OBIS (ranged from 1969 to 2025), 141 records fell in the western sector and only four in the eastern, whereas systematic survey recorded 39 on-effort sightings in the east. The sector almost absent from the opportunistic record. A further 45 OBIS records fell outside the three surveyed sectors entirely. The KDE map comparisson confiremed the spatial mismatch and the lack of records on the east side (@fig-kde_comp). Because opportunistic records carry no associated survey effort, these counts reflect where animals were reported rather than their relative density. The two datasets are therefore not directly comparable, and the systematic per-sector counts should be read alongside the effort-corrected encounter rates above (@tbl-spue_report).

![Opportunistic *Delphinus delphis* records from OBIS (squares) overlaid on the on-effort sightings recorded in the present study (circles), within the study area. Opportunistic records are concentrated in the western bay, while the eastern sector—almost absent from the opportunistic record, was covered only by systematic survey.](/figures/obis_comp.png){#fig-obis}

![KDE map from this study (A) and from the OBIS dataset (B) showed a strong discreptency of sighting density around the peninsula. The OBIS data suggests the 90% isopleth inside the Bay of Gibraltar while this study shows a distribution around the whole peninsula.](/figures/kde_comparison.png){#fig-kde_comp}

## Detection function fitting {#model_fit}
The distribution of sighting distances was examined separately for each station (@fig-dis_spot) to inform truncation and detection-function fitting. Sandy Bay and Prince George showed the distance distribution characteristic of point-transect sampling, in which detections are sparse close to the observer and rise to a peak before declining, reflecting the increase in surveyed area with radius alongside decreasing detectability [@bucklandDistanceSamplingMethods2015]. Europa Point departed from this pattern: detections were concentrated close to the observer and positively skewed, with few at greater range—consistent with its lower observation height (18 m a.s.l.), which restricts the effective detection range.

![Distribution of sighting distances (m) by observation station (A) and for the pooled dataset (B). Histograms were used to visually assess distance distributions and determine appropriate truncation distances. Dashed lines indicate the selected truncation distance for each station (bin width = 550 m).](figures/distance_facet.png){#fig-dis_spot}


Detection functions were fitted using the `Distance` package [@millerDistanceSampling2019] following a two-step procedure: the key function (half-normal or hazard-rate) was selected by AIC, and candidate covariates were evaluated in the second step. Functions were first fitted separately for each station. The hazard-rate key gave the lowest AIC at Europa Point and Sandy Bay, and the half-normal at Prince George, but per-station sample sizes were insufficient to support stable independent estimates (full per-station results in the Supplementary Material Section 3.4.1.).

A single pooled detection function was therefore fitted across all observations, following the same two-step procedure and right-truncated at 8,000 m. The distance retained all Europa Point detections while excluding the sparse long-distance tail at Sandy Bay. The hazard-rate key function gave the lower AIC (half-normal = `r round(AIC(d.hn)[1,2],2)`; hazard-rate = `r round(AIC(d.hr)[1,2],2)`) and adequate goodness of fit (Cramér–von Mises p = `r round(gof_hr$dsgof$CvM$p,3)`). Of the candidate covariates evaluated (glare, sea state, wave height, wind speed, and observation height), observation height gave the lowest AIC and was retained to accommodate between-station differences in detectability (@tbl-model_summary, @fig-ht_model).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model_summary
#| tbl-cap: "Model selection for the pooled detection function. The formula column indicates the covariate included in each candidate model; models are ranked by AIC."

tt(model_tab, digits = 3) %>% 
  style_tt(i = 0, bold = TRUE)

```


```{r}
#| label: fig-ht_model
#| fig-cap: "Pooled detection function (hazard-rate key function with observation height as a covariate)."
#| fig-height: 4

plot(d.ht, pdf = TRUE)
```



## Density and abundance estimates
Density was estimated from the pooled detection function (hazard-rate key with observation height as a covariate). The highest density occurred in the southern sector (surveyed from Europa Point), with a group density of `r round(sum_ht$dht$clusters$D$Estimate[1]* 1e6, 2)` groups km⁻² (95% CI: `r round(pool_group_dens[1,4], 2)`–`r round(pool_group_dens[1,5], 2)`; CV: `r round(pool_group_dens$CV[1], 2)`) and an individual density of `r round(sum_ht$dht$individuals$D$Estimate[1]* 1e6, 0)` individuals km⁻² (95% CI: `r round(pool_indiv_dens[1,4], 2)`–`r round(pool_indiv_dens[1,5], 2)`; CV: `r round(pool_indiv_dens$CV[1], 2)`) (@tbl-pool_dens). 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pool_dens
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of the density estimated for the pooled sightings. Density estimates (km⁻²) were derived from the best-fitting detection function for all three sampling locations. With standard error (SE), lower- and upper confidence limit (LCL/UCL) and coefficient of variance (CV). "

tt(pool_dens_tbl, digits = 2,
   width = c(2.5, 1.5, 1.5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1.5, 1, 1, 1, 1)) %>% 
  group_tt(j = list("Group Density (km⁻²)" = 3:7,   "Individual Density (km⁻²)" = 8:12)) %>% 
  style_tt(i = -2:0, bold = TRUE) %>% 
  style_tt(i = 4, bold = TRUE) %>% 
  style_tt(j = c(3, 8), line = "l", line_width = 0.1, line_color = "lightgrey")

```


Scaling these densities to the surveyed area at each station (the scanned sector to 8 km) yielded a covered-area abundance of `r round(sum_ht$dht$individuals$N$Estimate[1], 0)` individuals at Europa Point (95% CI: `r round(sum_ht$dht$individuals$N$lcl[1], 0)`–`r round(sum_ht$dht$individuals$N$ucl[1], 0)`; CV: `r round(sum_ht$dht$individuals$N$cv[1], 2)`), against `r round(sum_ht$dht$individuals$N$Estimate[2], 0)` and `r round(sum_ht$dht$individuals$N$Estimate[3], 0)` at Prince George and Sandy Bay respectively; because the fixed stations sampled only part of the territory and density was strongly spatially structured, these represent the surveyed areas rather than a territory-wide total and were not extrapolated to the full BGTW. The detection-corrected gradient reproduced the pattern seen in the raw encounter rate, with Europa Point exceeding the other sectors (@fig-SPUE). Per-station density and abundance estimates are reported in the Supplementary Material (Table S14 – S16).


```{r}
#| label: tbl-pool_abun
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of the relative abundance estimated for the pooled sightings. Relative abundance estimates were derived from the best-fitting detection function for the pooled sighting dataset. With standard error (SE), lower- and upper confidence limit (LCL/UCL) and coefficient of variance (CV)."

pool_abun_tbl %>% 
  select(c(1,2, 8:12)) %>% 
  tt(
   width = c(2.5, 1.5,1.5, 1, 1, 1, 1)) %>% 
  format_tt(j = 3:7, digits = 2) %>% 
  group_tt(j = list("Individual Abundance" = 3:7)) %>% 
  style_tt(i = -2:0, bold = TRUE) %>% 
  style_tt(i = 4, bold = TRUE) %>% 
  #style_tt(j = 3:7, align = "d") %>% 
  style_tt(j = c(3), line = "l", line_width = 0.1, line_color = "lightgrey")

```


### Truncation sensitivity test
To assess the influence of the right-truncation distance on the density estimates, the pooled detection function was refitted across a range of truncation distances (6,000-12,000 m) while holding the model structure (hazard-rate key function with height as a covariate) constant (Table S17). The selected truncation of 8,000 m retained 95% of on-effort detections (98 of 103) and yielded among the strongest goodness-of-fit values in the tested range, while excluding the sparse, high-variance long-distance tail that disproportionately influences point-transect estimates. The density and abundance estimates were therefore considered robust to the choice of truncation distance.
